source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Boot Time Post Package Repair with Correctable Errors
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. PPR Correctable Errors specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Runtime PPR > Row Sparing = Enable • This knob is not required to be enabled to test boot time PPR. It's only mentioned here because it was enabled when collecting the logs for this recipe. — Correctable Error Threshold = 1 — Trigger SW Error Threshold = Enable — SW Per Row Threshold = 2 • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — DDR PPR Type = Soft PPR — Attempt Fast Boot = Enable — Attempt Fast Cold Boot = Enable • If fast boot knobs are not enabled then BIOS will skip loading NVRAM and there'll be no PPR entries for boot time PPR. • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — RAS Log Level = MID (BASIC_FLOW, FUNC_FLOW) 1. Set up the system OS to capture FTrace/ELog record output per the ELOG BKM. >>> halt() >>> ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck() 2. Set the memDevs for a single-bit correctable error. Inject a correctable error then resume the system so BIOS can log the DIMM error record. >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1msk=0x0) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, sub_channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_rank=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, ps_ch=0, errType="ce") >>> go() 3. Observe in serial log that the SW Row Threshold counter is at 1/2. 4. Verify an ELog record was generated indicated by extlog_mem_event. 5. Repeat the last step so you reach the SW row threshold counter. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, sub_channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_rank=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, ps_ch=0, errType="ce") >>> go() 6. Confirm in serial log that the SW row threshold was reached. 7. Observe in serial log that BIOS qualified the bad row for PPR. 8. Verify that an ELog record was generated indicated by extmem_event_log. 9. Reboot the system and verify PPR action in the serial log. Observe that the DramMask is a non-zero value indication detection/correction of correctable errors. >>> itp.resettarget

disposition_reason: Boot-time PPR is causal across a reset: two events must hit one row, the second must cross the configured threshold, firmware must persist that row in NVRAM and the next boot must repair that same row. The exact coordinate, stage-specific serial/ELog records and reset continuity are therefore mandatory; extra injections would change the threshold experiment and are prohibited. test_case.test_name: Boot Time Post Package Repair with Correctable Errors — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that two correctable errors on the same intended GNR DRAM row reach the configured software threshold, cause BIOS to qualify that row, persist a boot-time Soft PPR request and complete repair with nonzero DramMask evidence.
required_package: GNR stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS and exact DIMM PN/serial/slot/DRAM-row topology
CScripts harness version/hash/license and memDevs/injector semantics
Project mapping/restoration for all BIOS/GRUB/PPR/fast-boot/threshold/DFX knobs
Exact coordinate and proof both injections reach the same row plus expected 1/2 and reached counters
Expected extlog_mem_event/extmem_event_log, qualification, DramMask and PprRepairStatus fields
Reset/reconnect/boot timeout, NVRAM persistence, crash/OOB recovery and no-retry plan
test_case.test_command: Record platform/DIMM topology, harness and BIOS baseline; map every source PPR/fast-boot/threshold knob and exact socket0/channel0/subchannel0/DIMM0/rank0/subrank0/bankgroup0/bank0/ps_ch0 row; preserve logs; execute only the approved memDevs setup and first CE, prove 1/2 plus extlog; execute the second identical CE, prove threshold reached, row qualification and extmem; run one approved `itp.resettarget`, retain continuous serial evidence through boot, correlate the same row and nonzero DramMask/PprRepairStatus, verify health, and restore settings.
test_case.expected_result: Serial log that the SW Row Threshold counter is at 1/2. ELog record was generated indicated by extlog_mem_event. Serial log that the SW row threshold was reached. Observe in serial log that BIOS qualified the bad row for PPR. ELog record was generated indicated by extmem_event_log.
